item.title: U-Haul worker allegedly shoots co-worker dead after argument during shift: Police
item.description: Devin Rice allegedly shot co-worker Fredrick Lytton multiple times during an argument over a drink at a Nashville U-Haul location, police say.
item.content:encoded:
A Nashville U-Haul employee allegedly gunned down his 56-year-old co-worker during a shift, as police say he fired several shots after the two men were arguing over a drink.

Devin Rice, 23, was arrested on Aug. 5 after he allegedly shot and killed Fredrick Lytton at a U-Haul store in Nashville, Tennessee, according to police. Lytton died after arriving at Vanderbilt University Medical Center.

The Metropolitan Nashville Police Department said Rice admitted to arguing with Lytton over a drink and then shooting him.

Police accused Rice of pulling out a pistol and shooting Lytton several times.

Officials said Rice fled the area after allegedly shooting Lytton, but was later arrested. Rice was arrested on charges of criminal homicide.

"The crime here in Nashville is getting really bad," Houghtaylen said. "Police need to do a better job at getting the guns off the street because there’s a lot of shootings in Nashville."

In a statement to Fox News Digital, Jeff Porter, U-Haul area district vice president of Tennessee, said, "We are shocked and deeply saddened by what occurred. Our concern right now is being there to support the victim’s family and our Team Members affected by this tragic event."

"Though Fred's life was taken too soon, his memories and the love he shared with family and friends will remain forever," the obituary said.

item.title: Fired Texas judge speaks out as dirty-water firestorm engulfs town
item.description: Jennifer Combs' Facebook post about Trinidad water led to her felony arrest, a fired judge, and a Texas Rangers investigation now rocking the city.
item.content:encoded:
When we first introduced you to Jennifer Combs, the facts already sounded hard to believe. The Texas mom said police arrested her after she used Facebook to collect complaints about discolored water in Trinidad.

Combs spent 23 hours in jail on a felony false alarm or report charge. A Henderson County grand jury later declined to indict her. She has since filed a federal lawsuit alleging political retaliation. You can read our original article on Jennifer Combs and the Trinidad, Texas water controversy.

Her arrest, however, did not end the controversy. Police later arrested a man who protested outside Trinidad City Hall. The judge who dismissed his charge says city officials fired her one week later.

TEXAS MOM JAILED OVER DIRTY WATER FACEBOOK POST

Former Trinidad Municipal Judge Shellena Bivens joined me on The CyberGuy Report podcast at CyberGuy.com to explain why she dismissed the protest case and what happened after that decision. Bivens had served as a judge for 16 years. She described herself in a way that was direct and deeply personal.

"I've been a damn good judge," Bivens said. "I've tried to be human."

The case involved Winston Noles, a citizen journalist known online as Otto the Watchdog. He went to Trinidad after learning about Combs' arrest. Noles stood outside city hall with a sign that used an expletive to criticize "bad cops." Trinidad police arrested him and charged him with misdemeanor disorderly conduct. The department's case centered on a claim that his sign had offended the city's water clerk. Bivens said the evidence presented to her did not support that charge.

Bivens recalled an officer entering her courtroom and presenting two possible outcomes. Police could take Noles to jail or bring him before her for arraignment. Her response was clear. "You need to let him go," Bivens said. "I said that multiple times. You need to let him go."

Bivens dismissed the disorderly conduct charge. She said Noles had not committed a crime by displaying the sign. Local reporting also found that the former water clerk, Colby Reyes, said in writing that Noles had not offended her. Reyes later joined another former city employee in a wrongful termination lawsuit against Trinidad.

The lawsuit alleges that city officials fired Reyes because she "refused to lie" about her reaction to the protest. Those allegations have not been proven in court. During our interview, Combs described the situation this way. "She would not sign a statement that said she was offended," Combs said. Then came the part that still seems unbelievable. "The judge dropped it. They fired the judge," Combs said.

CARIBBEAN HOT SPOT GRIPPED BY WATER CRISIS, AND TOURISTS SCRAMBLE TO RESCHEDULE PLANS

The Trinidad City Council voted 3-1 to dismiss Bivens during a May 28 meeting. Her attorney argued that the council's action was unlawful. The city proceeded with the dismissal. Bivens told me she returned to work and discovered she could no longer enter her office. "They changed my code when I came in to work on Tuesday," she said. "My security code was changed."

She said city leaders ended her 16-year judicial career without giving her a valid reason. When I asked whether she expected a Facebook post about water to cause this much upheaval, she answered quickly. "Absolutely not. No," Bivens said. "This has been such a crazy journey."

Bivens has said publicly that she believes the city retaliated against her because she dismissed Noles' charge. Her attorneys have considered legal action. The city has not admitted that retaliation motivated its vote.

CyberGuy sent a request for comment to the mayor and city council through the city’s published contact information but did not hear back before our deadline.

During our interview, Bivens also described an alleged conversation with Charles Gregory, who served as Trinidad's police chief when police arrested Combs. According to Bivens, Gregory entered her office after Combs published her Facebook post. "I know who it is, and I'm, I'm F-ing getting her. I'm getting her," Bivens recalled him saying.

That is Bivens' account of the conversation. CyberGuy has not independently verified that Gregory made the statement. Gregory previously defended the department's decision to pursue Combs. He said her Facebook post created "fear, panic, or unnecessary emergency response within a community." He later resigned, with June 19 reported as his final day.

We reached out to the Trinidad Police Department for comment about Bivens' allegations and the department's handling of the arrests. We did not hear back before our deadline.

In our earlier CyberGuy report, an attorney representing Trinidad said the city could not discuss details because of active lawsuits. "The claims against the City of Trinidad will be answered where they belong, in a court of law," attorney Zachary Smith wrote.

The warrant process later faced scrutiny from another judge. Henderson County District Judge R. Scott McKee approved the warrant connected to Combs' arrest. He later sent Gregory a letter questioning information that two Trinidad officers had presented. McKee questioned the "accuracy, completeness, and reliability" of the officers' information. According to the letter, the officers failed to disclose citizen complaints and water-quality concerns. They also left out information that could explain the basis for Combs' Facebook post.

McKee ordered the two officers to appear before him in person when seeking future warrants. They had previously been allowed to submit requests electronically. That development is important. A judge can only evaluate probable cause using the information police provide. Missing context may change how a judge views the entire case.

Meanwhile, state investigators confirmed that Trinidad's water system had real problems. The Texas Commission on Environmental Quality released findings from two investigations on July 1. The first investigation found that Trinidad's system failed to meet state minimums involving total chlorine and iron. The report said the system had returned to compliance by April 22 after a boil-water notice.

A second investigation began on May 15. It resulted in four violations. Investigators documented problems with required chloramine-effectiveness sampling. They also found maintenance issues at the surface water treatment plant. In one sample, investigators recorded 20 color units. The EPA and TCEQ recommend a maximum of 15 color units. These findings do not confirm every medical claim posted online. However, they show that residents were raising concerns about a system with documented deficiencies.

Combs and Bivens also discussed a Trinidad family that said its 16-year-old daughter developed a serious skin reaction after showering. Medical records obtained by a local TV station described the condition as "most likely chemical burn/severe dermatitis from water she was exposed to." However, the report also stated that it remained unclear whether Trinidad's water-treatment process caused the reaction. The family was considering legal action at the time of the report.

Bivens told me she knew the family and had seen photographs of the teenager's injuries. "I've seen the pictures," Bivens said. "I know the family of the young girl that got burned." The family's allegation and the medical assessment deserve attention. Still, a final legal or regulatory determination about the cause has not been made.

On July 10, the Texas Rangers confirmed that they had opened an investigation involving Trinidad. "We can confirm the Texas Rangers are investigating," the agency told Dallas affiliate FOX 4. Because the investigation remains active, the Rangers did not disclose its scope.

Then, on July 16, all three members of Trinidad's city hall staff resigned. The departing officials were City Manager Cynthia Dosier, City Clerk Sandra Rojas and Municipal Judge Susan Carver. Carver had taken over the municipal judge position after Bivens' dismissal. Mayor Dennis Haws warned that the resignations would create operational problems while the city worked through the transition. The resignations do not prove wrongdoing. They do show how far this controversy has spread since Combs published her original Facebook post.

Combs says people associated with a small group in Trinidad mass-reported her Facebook post. The platform then removed it. During our interview, Bivens directed a message at Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg. "Stop trampling on people's rights," Bivens said. "Stop trampling on free speech." We reached out to Meta for comment on Bivens' message, but did not hear back before our deadline.

Facebook's content-moderation system did not arrest Combs. Still, removing a post can erase evidence of what someone said and how other people responded. That is why screenshots matter. Save the original post and relevant comments when documenting a public concern. Keep copies of notices or messages you receive from officials.

You should also separate confirmed facts from reports that still need verification. Phrases such as "residents reported" or "we are asking the state to investigate" make that distinction clear. For more ways to control what social platforms collect and preserve your account security, see our five simple tech tips to take back control of social media.

Jennifer Combs says she used Facebook to gather water complaints from people who felt ignored. Police responded with a felony charge, yet a grand jury declined to indict her. Winston Noles then protested her treatment. Judge Shellena Bivens dismissed his disorderly conduct charge because she said the evidence did not support it. Trinidad's City Council fired her one week later. Since then, another judge has questioned the police warrant process. State investigators have documented water-system violations. The Texas Rangers are also investigating, although they have not revealed the scope. Public officials have every right to correct false information. They also have a duty to respect lawful criticism. Arresting people who question local government creates a chilling effect that can reach far beyond one small town. For more on how this controversy unfolded, check out the full conversation with Judge Bivens on The CyberGuy Report podcast at CyberGuy.com.

When a Facebook post about dirty water can lead to two arrests, a fired judge and a Texas Rangers investigation, how safe would you feel speaking up in your own community? Let us know by writing to us at CyberGuy.com.

item.title: 3 dead, including child, in 'domestic-related homicide' at Minneapolis-area daycare: police
item.description: Hopkins Police Chief Brent Johnson said three people, including a child, were found dead inside a daycare after officers responded to a domestic call.
item.content:encoded:
Three people, including a child, have been found dead in a "domestic-related homicide" at an in-home daycare near Minneapolis on Wednesday, police said.

If you or someone you know is having thoughts of suicide, please contact the National Suicide Prevention Lifeline at 1-800-273-TALK (8255).

Hopkins Police Chief Brent Johnson said officers responded to a report of a domestic situation around 9 a.m. at the Brown Bear Daycare and discovered a man, woman and child deceased inside the home, according to Fox 9 Minneapolis-St. Paul. All three victims are believed to be family members and the six other children in the facility at the time of the incident, who were unharmed, have been reunited with their families, he reportedly added.

Johnson said a parent who showed up at the daycare to drop off a child called police and investigators believe that parent witnessed the incident, the station reported.

"There's no worse scenario than this, where you drop off your child to somewhere you think is safe, and you get that phone call," Johnson was quoted as saying. "I think we can all relate, [those] who have children and those who don't. This is just a tragic situation anywhere in the world, let alone here in Hopkins."

2 CUSTODIANS DEAD IN POSSIBLE MURDER-SUICIDE AT CHICAGO ELEMENTARY SCHOOL

The Hopkins Police Department later released a statement to Fox News Digital saying it "responded to a report of a stabbing at a residence operating as a home daycare in the 200 block of Tyler Avenue North in Hopkins."

"At this time, we believe there are no outstanding suspects and no ongoing threat to the public," police added. "This is an extremely tragic event for our community. Our thoughts and prayers are with the families affected by this devastating incident."

"I know that our hearts and our prayers are with the people of Hopkins and any families that have been impacted," Minneapolis Mayor Jacob Frey said Wednesday, according to the station. "I have already touched base directly with Hanlon and offer any assistance we can provide. The City of Minneapolis stands with Hopkins. We are not strangers to crisis, and when it takes place, we work together. That’s exactly what we’ll be doing here."

"We’re aware of this morning’s tragic and devastating incident in Hopkins and are working with Hopkins Police as they investigate," added Hennepin County Attorney Mary Moriarty. "Our office’s victim services division is prepared to support the individuals impacted by this incident."

item.title: Hasan Piker warns ‘the knives will be out’ after socialist Francesca Hong falls in Wisconsin upset
item.description: Hasan Piker warned "the knives will be out" for socialists after Francesca Hong lost the Wisconsin Democratic gubernatorial primary to David Crowley.
item.content:encoded:
Far-left streamer Hasan Piker warned Tuesday night that "the knives will be out" for the socialist left after Wisconsin state Rep. Francesca Hong lost the Democratic gubernatorial primary to Milwaukee County Executive David Crowley.

Pike argued during his livestream that Democratic establishment figures will work harder to stop insurgent candidates because they no longer underestimate the progressive movement.

Piker, who appeared alongside Hong and Rep. Ilhan Omar, D-Minn., at an August campaign rally, portrayed the loss as a warning for socialists seeking to build on recent primary victories.

"It will be more difficult, though, because the establishment will not underestimate us. It will continue to undermine us, but they will not underestimate us," Piker said. "So, the knives will be out."

HASAN PIKER CALLS FOR DEMOCRATS WHO OPPOSE ABDUL EL-SAYED TO BE 'PUNISHED'

RNC national spokesperson Natalie Baldassarre responded to Piker's remarks in a statement to Fox News Digital on Wednesday, calling on Democrats to disavow the controversial streamer.

"Hasan Piker is a Hamas-hugging radical with a long history of threatening rape and violence against those he disagrees with. Democrats would do right to disavow him, but they'll continue to bend to his will like spineless, useful idiots," Baldassarre said.

The Wisconsin primary became a contest between the party’s socialist left and its more traditional coalition. Hong, a Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) member, was backed by Reps. Ilhan Omar, D-Minn., and Ro Khanna, D-Calif., former Ohio state Sen. Nina Turner and Wisconsin-based DSA chapters.

After initially leaving the race, Crowley reentered the contest with the endorsement of retiring Democratic Gov. Tony Evers and accumulated support from the Professional Firefighters of Wisconsin, the Wisconsin Laborers’ District Council, the IBEW Wisconsin State Conference and a slate of Democratic mayors and local officials.

DEMOCRATIC ESTABLISHMENT STRIKES BACK AS SOCIALIST CANDIDATE DOWNED IN BATTLEGROUND PRIMARY

Hong previously sought to put distance between herself and Piker after appearing on his livestream for a campaign fundraiser, saying in a July "MS NOW Reports" interview that sharing a platform with someone did not mean she endorsed everything the host had said.

Former Los Angeles mayoral candidate and TV personality Spencer Pratt mocked the reaction of Piker and the DSA following Hong’s defeat.

"Beetlejuice Bob isn’t take the Hong loss well," Pratt said on X. "The DSA are freaking out that everyone is realizing Emperor Mao here has no clothes."

Piker said Crowley’s victory was "far from the worst result" and predicted the Democrat would defeat Republican Rep. Tom Tiffany in November.

‘COMMON SENSE AGAINST CRAZY’: TRUMP-BACKED CANDIDATE SOUNDS ALARM ON SOCIALIST HONG IN WISCONSIN RACE

"Crowley still, if he wins, is going to defeat Tom Tiffany. And that's a good thing. OK, I stand on that," Piker said.

The Wisconsin Democratic gubernatorial primary was not called until early Wednesday after Milwaukee election officials said "human error" delayed the county's vote count. 

Five of nine memory sticks delivered to the Milwaukee County Courthouse contained audit logs instead of election results after an election worker pushed the wrong button, according to Milwaukee Election Commission Director Paulina Gutierrez.

Fox News Digital reached out to Hong, Crowley and the DNC for comment, but did not immediately receive a response.

item.title: Luigi Mangione hearing set for Friday stirs plea deal speculation in his federal case
item.description: Luigi Mangione's defense and federal prosecutors jointly requested a conference for Friday, fueling plea deal speculation ahead of his state murder trial.
item.content:encoded:
Justice Department prosecutors and defense attorneys for accused assassin Luigi Mangione asked a U.S. judge Tuesday to set a conference for Friday morning, prompting speculation the 28-year-old could agree to a plea deal in his federal case days before he's scheduled to go to trial on state murder charges.

Neither side immediately responded to requests for comment from Fox News Digital after an anonymous ABC report said the purpose of the hearing was for the sides to discuss a potential agreement.

A two-sentence letter for the judge requesting the hearing makes no mention of a purpose.

LUIGI MANGIONE JUDGE SAYS JURORS WILL REMAIN ANONYMOUS AFTER THREATS AND HARASSMENT OF WITNESSES

"The parties write jointly to request a conference with the Court," it reads. "Based on communications with Chambers, we understand that the Court is available to hold the conference on Friday, August 14, 2026, at 11:00 a.m."

Mangione is accused of stalking UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson, 50, and shooting him in the back outside a New York City Hilton hotel in December 2024.

Jury selection in the state case is set for Sept. 8, and the federal trial is tentatively expected to kick off in early 2027.

In July, Manhattan prosecutors responded to earlier reports of a potential plea deal in a letter to New York Judge Gregory Carro.

"The People are aware of public reporting regarding the possibility of a guilty plea in defendant's federal case," assistant DA Joel Seidemann wrote.

"If a proposed federal guilty plea would operate to defeat a just outcome in the state prosecution, the People could advise the federal district court of that consequence, and the court should consider that fact in deciding whether to accept the plea, as well as any opposition by the victim's family to such a resolution."

Carro issued an order Tuesday protecting the identities and addresses of jurors in the upcoming case, finding that witnesses have been threatened, doxxed and harassed already and that "individuals identifying themselves as supporters of the defendant engaged in inflammatory and hostile public statements outside the courthouse and announced their intention to attend jury selection to attempt to speak to prospective jurors."

Prosecutors had requested the move.

The defense has separately asked for the trial to be livestreamed, which experts have said is unlikely under current New York law.

Mangione has pleaded not guilty to all charges.

He faces a maximum sentence of 25 years to life in prison on the state charges if convicted, and up to life without parole federally.

item.title: Freed Marine returns home 'very frail' after Russian 'nightmare' as family advocate urges Trump to free others
item.description: Robert Gilman was unable to walk off the plane after more than 1,660 days in Russian custody and now faces an extensive physical and mental recovery.
item.content:encoded:
After more than 1,660 days in Russian custody, U.S. Marine veteran Robert Gilman is finally home — but new details about his deteriorated health following the yearslong "nightmare" suggest his ordeal is far from over.

"He's very frail," Kieran Ramsey, a representative for the Gilman family, told "America's Newsroom" on Wednesday.

"If you've seen any of the photos that the White House has since released, you can see just how frail he is."

AMERICAN EX-MARINE FEARED NEAR DEATH AFTER WEEKS IN CATATONIC STATE IN RUSSIAN PRISON

Gilman, who was released from Russian captivity Tuesday, was unable to walk off the plane on his own, Ramsey said. He will also require extensive mental and psychological care, along with physical and dental treatment, as he begins what is expected to be a lengthy recovery.

Massachusetts Democratic Sen. Ed Markey, who worked on Gilman's case, also blamed Russia on Tuesday while stating that the complete details of Gilman's condition remain unknown.

He shared that Gilman had been subjected to "physical torture, forced medication and provocations by the Russian government."

"This was an over 1,600-day nightmare that this man lived through," Ramsey echoed. "This former Marine, this fellow American, was subjected to severe physical abuse if not torture, mental abuse, mental torture. We just can't even imagine it."

US MARINE VETERAN RELEASED FROM RUSSIAN PRISON AFTER 1,666 DAYS OF DETENTION

Gilman's ordeal began after traveling to Russia while en route to Moldova. Per reports, Gilman became seriously ill during the trip and was later arrested on charges of assaulting police officers — allegations that many have characterized as false.

Ramsey said Gilman's case fits a broader pattern of Russia targeting Americans, including former U.S. Marines, and then piling additional charges onto detainees once they are in custody.

He pointed to the cases of fellow Marine veterans Trevor Reed and Paul Whelan as examples, urging officials to bring any remaining Americans home.

"Unfortunately, Robert's case is no different. And the tragic thing is, we have at least ten other Americans, five of whom my firm represents, that are also facing the same thing, and we really need to get these folks home," he said.

Ramsey credited Trump for Gilman's return later in the segment, reiterating his hope that the president and special envoy Steve Witkoff will work to free those who remain overseas.

item.title: Boater scared off alligator, then used rope to stop bleeding after Florida woman lost arm
item.description: A boater used rope from his vehicle as a makeshift tourniquet after an alligator grabbed a swimmer's arm in Florida's Silver River and pulled her underwater.
item.content:encoded:
The woman who lost her right arm in a vicious alligator attack in Florida on Saturday has been identified as Dina Rae Spann.

The attack happened Saturday afternoon in the Silver River in Marion County, where Spann was swimming with a group, the New York Post reported.

Spann, 58, was trying to keep the alligator's mouth closed while making her way toward the surface for air, her son, Zach Guerrina, told the news outlet.

FLORIDA WOMAN LOSES ARM IN SILVER RIVER ALLIGATOR ATTACK AS BOATER RACES TO SAVE HER LIFE

"It had her, but she said she was trying to make sure it didn’t get to her legs," he said. 

Spann also suffered an injury to her left hand during the struggle, losing part of her ring finger, Guerrina said. Her right arm was ultimately amputated below the elbow.

Nearby, John Gamache, a longtime visitor to the Silver Springs area, and his father were having lunch on their boat when they heard people yelling for help.

"I looked just upriver from us a couple hundred feet and saw an alligator head way above the water and going full speed towards the swimmers," Gamache told FOX 35 Orlando.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

Gamache quickly headed toward the group in his boat. 

By the time he reached the swimmers, the alligator had released Spann — and the activity from the approaching boat appeared to drive the animal away, according to the outlet.

He found Spann holding onto a paddleboard with a severe arm injury. He took rope from his boat and used it as a makeshift tourniquet to help control the bleeding.

"It was a terrible injury, bones poking out, blood everywhere," Gamache said. "Obviously, the minutes mattered."

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Despite the severity of her injuries, Guerrina said his mother remained remarkably calm as those around her worked to help.

After helping the other swimmers onto the boat, Gamache and his father took the group to a nearby boat launch, where first responders were waiting.

Spann was transported to a hospital following the attack. 

By Sunday, her family said she was back home and in good spirits despite losing her right arm, according to FOX 35 Orlando.

In the aftermath of the attack, authorities temporarily closed the Silver River while wildlife officials searched the area.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE STORIES

A contracted nuisance alligator trapper removed a 9-foot-8-inch alligator on Sunday, according to the Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission. Officials later lifted the temporary closure of the river.

The attack was unlike anything Gamache had witnessed there before, he said.

Spann's family later contacted him to thank him for coming to her aid.

"They called earlier, and we talked for a while, and it was heartwarming to hear them explain their emotions," Gamache said.

"We're glad that it happened as good as it could have," he added. 

"The result is just the sustained injury and nothing more."

item.title: Jewish Dem defections threaten El-Sayed in Michigan Senate race decided by razor-thin margins
item.description: Some Jewish voters in Michigan say they may cross party lines to support Mike Rogers over Abdul El-Sayed in the Senate election due to concerns over antisemitism and Israel.
item.content:encoded:
Jewish voters could provide the decisive margin in Michigan’s November Senate election, particularly as some lifelong Democrats say they are prepared to cross party lines and vote for Republican Mike Rogers against Democrat Abdul El-Sayed.

Analysts point to Michigan’s last U.S. Senate race decided by just 19,006 votes. With estimates placing the state’s Jewish population between approximately 105,000 and 130,000 adults, those votes could tip the scales in favor of Rogers.

"Republicans made real gains in the most Jewish areas in 2024, and Michigan was no exception," Matthew Knee, a Republican pollster and consultant who serves as chief data officer of Pulse Decision Science, told Fox News Digital.

"Stevens massively outperformed in many Jewish precincts as well," Knee said, commenting on the primary. "Rogers and El-Sayed are both the kinds of candidates that will accelerate this trend. There are only 130,000 Jewish voters in Michigan, but in 2024, Rogers only lost by 19,006 votes, so that can make the difference in that kind of razor-thin environment."

DEM ATTORNEY BACKS GOP HOPEFUL IN MICHIGAN RACE AGAINST EL-SAYED, 'JUMPING SHIP' FROM HIS PARTY'S 'LUNATICS'

For generations, voting for the Democratic Party has been part of the identity of many Jewish families across the state, but since El-Sayed’s victory, some are moving toward the Republican Party.

In interviews with Fox News Digital, several Jewish Michigan voters said El-Sayed’s positions regarding Israel and Zionism have forced them to choose between the liberal values they have supported throughout their lives and what they view as the safety of their children and community.

For many, that prospective vote would not represent a wholesale rejection of the Democratic Party. It would be a break in this single race, a split-ticket vote they once considered unthinkable.

Steve Cohen, a lifelong Michigan resident and self-described "notorious ticket splitter," said the current political climate has made the Senate race especially consequential.

"We’ve had attacks on our synagogues and our school buildings where our kids go," Cohen said. "There’s a torrent of activity pushing anti-Israel and anti-Jewish things on our campuses, and that includes every part of the state of Michigan. So, right now, it’s a little bit scary to be a Jew here."

LEFT-WING ACTIVISTS HECKLE PRO-ISRAEL DEMOCRAT HALEY STEVENS AT MICHIGAN CONVENTION

"I now feel forced to choose between those liberal values and the safety of my children," said Benji, a lifelong Michigan resident and self-identified liberal whose last name Fox News Digital is withholding for security reasons.

"As a lifelong Jewish liberal, I have advocated for liberal values, including commonsense gun laws, LGBT rights, women’s reproductive healthcare, healthcare reform and Black Lives Matter," Benji said.

"El-Sayed may claim to love Jews and the Jewish people, but requiring Jews to be anti-Zionist is a racist purity test and makes his claim ring hollow," he added. "I believe in changing the system from within, but it is no longer safe inside that system for me or for my children."

Stacy, who also asked to withhold her last name, comes from a fifth-generation Democratic Jewish family and has lived in Michigan for 13 years. She has also never voted Republican. Her alienation from the Democratic Party intensified at its state convention in April, where she said she felt hostility toward anyone who openly supported Israel.

"I felt the hatred and hostility in the room toward me if I dared to be supportive of Israel," Stacy said. She recalled watching Stevens being booed and harassed and said she "could see the writing on the wall."

"I take no joy in feeling like my party has abandoned me, but I need to vote this way for self-preservation," she said.

Stacy also pointed to Rogers’ experience, calling him the more qualified candidate "if you look at it just on paper."

Mike Rogers is a former Army officer, FBI special agent, congressman and chairman of the House Intelligence Committee.

Jewish voters make up approximately 1.4% of Michigan’s electorate, representing an estimated 105,000 people statewide, according to the American Jewish Population Project at Brandeis University. Much of the community is concentrated in the politically significant Detroit suburbs.

"We hear constantly about the Muslim vote in Michigan, particularly in Dearborn, as a crucial political bloc. But the truth is that Jews in the Great Lakes State are a comparably sized religious minority and historically a much more important constituency for the Democratic Party," said Jesse Arm, Manhattan Institute vice president and pollster.

BIDEN-WORLD VETERAN ISSUES STARK WARNING ABOUT ABDUL EL-SAYED AS HE CROSSES PARTY LINES

Arm said Jewish voters turn out at high rates and have long provided Democratic candidates with votes and financial support. He said Jewish organizers and political fundraisers described "an unprecedented level of opposition to El-Sayed among Jewish Democrats."

"Some intend simply to withhold their votes and contributions," Arm said. "But many prominent Jewish Democratic families and donors are prepared to go further and directly support Mike Rogers."

Sam Markstein, national political director and spokesman for the Republican Jewish Coalition, told Fox News Digital those voters could provide the decisive margin in November.

Markstein said the RJC analyzed primary results in Oak Park, Bloomfield Township, West Bloomfield and Southfield, four Oakland County communities with sizable Jewish populations. According to the organization’s analysis, Stevens received approximately 37,000 votes across those communities, compared with about 20,000 for El-Sayed.

Her combined 17,000-vote advantage was greater than the statewide margin by which Rogers lost his 2024 Senate campaign to Democrat Elissa Slotkin.

"That’s a really big delta there that shows that Jewish voters do not like Abdul El-Sayed," Markstein said.

He called Michigan’s Jewish voters "not just a rounding error" and said Republicans have an opportunity to move more of them into their column in November.

Markstein also criticized El-Sayed’s response to the March terrorist attack at Temple Israel in West Bloomfield. An armed attacker rammed a vehicle into the synagogue, where approximately 140 children were present, before opening fire. No children, congregants or staff members were physically harmed.

FBI NABS 7 FOR ALLEGED 'CAMPAIGN OF VIOLENCE' TO PRESSURE UNIVERSITY OF MICHIGAN, BUSINESSES OVER ISRAEL TIES

El-Sayed initially condemned the attack as "heinous" but later faced criticism after discussing violence in the Middle East while reflecting on the attacker’s actions and saying "hurt people do hurt people."

El-Sayed has maintained that he condemns antisemitism and is committed to protecting Michigan’s Jewish community.

Fox News Digital reached out to El-Sayed’s campaign regarding the concerns raised by the Jewish voters who were interviewed but did not receive a response.

However, in a previous statement on concerns over antisemitism, El-Sayed stated in May, "I understand what it’s like to be discriminated against for how I pray. This is why I will always stand against antisemitism and stand with my Jewish brothers and sisters and their right to practice their faith safely, freely and unabashedly."

Fox News Digital reached out to the Michigan Democratic Jewish Caucus for comment but did not receive a response. In a statement issued after the primary, however, the caucus congratulated El-Sayed on his victory while acknowledging "frustration, anxiety and deep disappointment" among Jewish Democrats and calling on the nominee to engage directly with Michigan’s Jewish community.

The caucus said El-Sayed must "address the harm caused during this campaign," arguing his repeated focus on organized Jewish political participation had "crossed an alarming line." At the same time, it urged concerned Jewish Democrats not to abandon the party, saying their place in the Democratic coalition remains "indispensable."

Arm cautioned that Rogers should not take the voting bloc for granted.

"Rogers shouldn’t assume he has it in the bag," Arm said. "El-Sayed is telegenic, disciplined and politically crafty, and he’ll spend the months between now and November looking for ways to present himself as more heterodox and less radical than the record suggests."

The Jewish Federation of Detroit directed Fox News Digital to a statement it released after the primary election result, while noting that, as a 501(c)(3), it "cannot and does not endorse or oppose candidates."

SIGN UP FOR ANTISEMITISM EXPOSED NEWSLETTER

"As an organization, we will continue to engage across the political spectrum to advocate for issues essential to our future, including standing against antisemitism, violence and bigotry, ensuring the safety and security of the Jewish community and houses of worship, and championing Israel as a Jewish and democratic state," the statement said.

Rabbi Aaron Starr of Congregation Shaarey Zedek in suburban Detroit said the concerns extend beyond any single candidate.

"American Jews have long rejected extremism, particularly within our political parties," Starr told Fox News Digital. "We reject extremism on the right, and we reject extremism on the left. 

"Right now, however, it feels as though extremism on the left is not only becoming louder, but increasingly normalized. That has created a frightening moment for American Jews and certainly for the Jewish community here in Michigan."

For Benji and Stacy, the possibility of voting Republican does not mean they have stopped believing in the causes they have supported for decades. It means that, for the first time, they believe their Democratic values and their safety as Jews have been placed in conflict.

Voting for a Republican was once unthinkable. Following El-Sayed’s nomination, they say it now feels unavoidable.

item.title: Marine veteran Robert Gilman returns to US soil as Trump admin fulfills request: 'No American left behind'
item.description: Photos show Robert Gilman arriving on U.S. soil, where he was met by Steve Witkoff and Sebastian Gorka after the Trump administration secured his release.
item.content:encoded:
Photos and video emerged Wednesday showing Marine veteran Robert Gilman back on American soil following his release from Russian custody.

Gilman, a U.S. citizen who was arrested on Jan. 17, 2022, in Voronezh, Russia, and sentenced to a total of 10 years in prison, was freed on humanitarian grounds Tuesday after 1,666 days in prison. President Donald Trump said Gilman would land at Andrews Air Force Base in Washington, D.C., on Tuesday night, and after speaking with him, "he had one request — A GREAT cheeseburger when he lands."

"Our Marine is safely back on American soil," Sebastian Gorka, a deputy assistant to the president, wrote on X early Wednesday, sharing a video of an aircraft coming to a stop. "As President Donald Trump promised, Steve Witkoff brought Robert Gilman cheeseburgers and milkshakes!"

US MARINE VETERAN RELEASED FROM RUSSIAN PRISON AFTER 1,666 DAYS OF DETENTION

"(I snuck him a cigar for when he’s fully recovered!)," Gorka added. "And a member of our broader White House team brought him his own USMC flag. There are very few jobs like this one. No American left behind."

In his own post, Witkoff, who is the U.S. special envoy to the Middle East, said it was a "special night welcoming an American citizen home to his family and country."

"Thank you POTUS for never leaving anyone behind," Witkoff also said, sharing an image of him and Gorka alongside Gilman on the plane following the landing.

"Robert is a patriot — a former United States Marine who served our country with honor. He can now finally return to his family and receive the medical care he needs," Witkoff said in a separate post. "His return is another testament to POTUS’s extraordinary leadership and unwavering commitment to bringing Americans home. Under his leadership, Marc Fogel and Ksenia Karelina were also brought home from Russia."

AMERICAN EX-MARINE FEARED NEAR DEATH AFTER WEEKS IN CATATONIC STATE IN RUSSIAN PRISON

Gilman was convicted in 2022 of assaulting a police officer, initially receiving a sentence of three and a half years. Gilman’s troubles in custody then increased in 2024 when he was found guilty by Russia of attacking a prison inspector during a cell check, assaulting an investigator and beating another guard.

In December 2025, Russia once again extended Gilman's prison sentence after a regional court found him guilty of a new assault on prison staff.

However, the U.S. State Department referred to Gilman as a wrongful detainee.

Gilman is the third U.S. Marine to be taken prisoner in Russia in the last decade, following Russia's detention of Paul Whelan in 2018 and Trevor Reed in 2019. Both were later released in prisoner swaps.

"After my discussions with President Vladimir Putin, Russia has agreed to release him, very much on a Humanitarian Basis. We appreciate this decision, and the fact that Russia asked for no one in return — No exchange took place," Trump wrote Tuesday on Truth Social.

"Robert Gilman has been reunited with his wonderful mother, Nancy, who is also on the plane with him, and will soon get to see all of his loved ones," Trump added.

Fox News’ Emma Bussey, Robert McGreevy, Gillian Turner, Nick Kalman and Louis Casiano contributed to this post.

item.title: ‘Grease’ star Stockard Channing says she’s ‘happy being a recluse’ after leaving America
item.description: Stockard Channing revealed her reclusive London lifestyle, morning routine with her dog and why her longtime partner's death shifted everything.
item.content:encoded:
Stockard Channing admitted she's "happy being a recluse" as she reflected on her quiet lifestyle after fleeing the states for the United Kingdom.

The "Grease" star began living in London "just before COVID," a move she envisioned after the 2014 death of her partner of 25 years, producer Daniel Gilham.

"I've lived alone since I lost Daniel and I'm happy being a recluse," Channing wrote in an essay for The Sunday Times. "I was married four times before Daniel, and they all represent epochs of me.

HEATHER LOCKLEAR SAYS SHE LIVES 'FAR AWAY' FROM HOLLYWOOD AND STAYS OUT OF THE SOCIAL SCENE

"I grew up in the sixties, reacting to that repressed notion of marriage and sexuality from the fifties kinda like Rizzo," she noted. "Children were thought about and, yeah, I think about them now because it'd be great to have someone taking care of me. But, hey, children can be just as selfish as everybody else out there."

Channing, 82, confessed that Gilham's death "was more devastating than I realized; it had a lag effect."

‘SOPRANOS’ STAR JAMIE-LYNN SIGLER FLED HOLLYWOOD FOR TEXAS WHERE SHE NO LONGER FEELS ‘WATCHED’

"The pattern of my life shifted, so I shifted my life from Maine," she wrote of the move, which also vaguely coincided with Trump's second presidential bid.

"When I started playing 'The West Wing's first lady, Abbey Bartlet, in 1999, we were about to move to the second Bush administration," she wrote. "The cast had a good look at that Washington world, and there seemed to be a level of honest, intelligent discourse that is missing from 2026.

"People look at 'The West Wing' and go, 'Wow, wasn't it great when politicians had an ounce of integrity?' Abbey didn't suffer fools, and she's the character most like me in real life."

Channing reflected on an interaction with director Aaron Sorkin, who said he "wrote Abbey as the person he saw in me."

"I was quite short with him the first time we met," she wrote. "He was saying all these nice things, and I said, 'Look, I don't have time for flattery.' I didn't mean to be rude it was just one of those days."

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

Her days of stardom are slightly different from now as the "Six Degrees of Separation" actress detailed her morning routine, which begins at 7 a.m. when her dog wakes her up.

"After he's had his breakfast and I've made a strong pot of coffee, my dog walker takes him out and I go back to bed," she wrote. "My ideal morning."

"My duvet is covered in ink spots because for many years I've been keeping a diary. I sit there with my fountain pen and my thoughts. What do I feel about this or that?

"I only leave the bed when I need to go to the bathroom. At my age life is guided by bodily functions."

By 10 a.m., Channing pursues a "bit of exercise," but admitted that her "favorite exercise days are when I play hooky."

"I know that exercising is the right thing to do but my brain tells me to go hide behind the bike sheds," she wrote. "Lunch is my first meal of the day and I can follow a recipe, but if my ramen doesn't work out I give it to the dog.

"If I'm leaving the apartment I comb my hair, but I don't have a wardrobe of designer outfits. Well, I do, but they're all from the Eighties and Nineties. Do I care how I look? Most actors do although part of your job is not being self-conscious.

"But I've never considered myself as beautiful. And I'm not a celebrity 'tart.' I'm just me, take it or leave it."

Channing's fan base is vast, and she recognized how different age groups remember her as different characters.

"For younger girls it's 'Practical Magic,' for grown-ups it's 'The West Wing,' and for real grown-ups it's 'Grease,'" she wrote. "Although the critics weren't kind about Grease, it made tons of money and it still gets streamed a lot.

"I guess films are like songs: they take you back to a particular time in your life. Maybe a more innocent time."

item.content:encoded:
The "decoy" Air Force One that President Donald Trump was snuck off of was protected by U.S. fighter jets on its flight to the United Kingdom, a senior Trump administration official told Fox News on Wednesday.

The revelation pushes back on media fears the press corps and staff might have been left vulnerable to the perceived threat from hostile actors seeking to strike Trump's flight out of Ankara, Turkey, last month.

The previously undisclosed security measure adds another layer to the extraordinary precautions surrounding the president’s plane swap, which left the aircraft normally associated with Trump continuing on to the U.K. without him aboard.

The press corps was joined on the "decoy" plane under U.S. fighter jet cover by Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, and were aware Trump was not on board, the official said.

TRUMP USED CATERING TRUCK, AIR FORCE ONE DECOY TO EVADE IRAN THREAT: REPORT

White House staff and reporters boarded the original plane as normal, where bags of snack mix bearing the presidential seal were waiting for them.

TRUMP’S SLY PLANE SWITCH RAISES EYEBROWS OVER SAFETY OF PASSENGERS LEFT BEHIND ON BOARD

Once aboard, however, the press was told to keep the window shades down. A Secret Service agent later came to the press cabin to reinforce the instruction, according to the pool report. When a photographer briefly opened a shade, the photographer was quickly told to close it again.

"They wanted me to go on a different flight, a different plane, equal safety — but they wanted me to do it, so I do it. I do what they say."

item.title: DOJ heavyweights throw monkey wrench in Dem plans to put Trump allies in hot seat
item.description: President Donald Trump's private advisors can now claim executive privilege under a new Justice Department memo, and Democrats vow investigations.
item.content:encoded:
President Donald Trump's private advisors and attorneys are now protected by executive privilege as long as their conversations relate to the president's official decision-making, according to a memo Tuesday from the Justice Department's Office of Legal Counsel.

"The need for presidential confidentiality applies to communications with private advisers just as it does with government officials," the 21-page memo stated.

The memo, written by Assistant Attorney General Elliot Gaiser, comes months ahead of the midterm elections as Democrats battle for control of Congress. 

Democrats have pledged to continue their investigations into Trump and his family's business dealings and financial investments, potentially using subpoenas and congressional hearings to advance those probes.

TRUMP AG PICK TODD BLANCHE FACES SENATE TEST IN FIRST MAJOR CONFIRMATION FIGHT SINCE GRAHAM’S DEATH

Under the Office of Legal Counsel's new nonbinding memo, private citizens who have offered advice in confidential conversations with Trump or White House staffers about official presidential duties can claim executive privilege if they're subpoenaed by Congress.

"The presidential communications privilege is rooted in the need for confidentiality to ensure that [this] presidential decision-making is of the highest caliber, informed by honest advice and full knowledge," the memo stated. "Without a promise of confidentiality, the President’s ability to ‘decide and act quickly’ on matters of unrivaled importance would be seriously hindered."

The memo noted that the president may sometimes need expertise and guidance from an outside source who could be crucial to making the best decision. Gaiser also acknowledged that a private advisor to the president may be more hesitant to offer guidance because of concerns that doing so could negatively affect the advisor's livelihood.

"Such individuals may be reluctant to provide advice on controversial or unpopular policies based on a fear of public disclosure or potential ramifications for their personal endeavors," the memo stated.

Gaiser pointed to a long history of presidents seeking advice from people outside the federal government. Andrew Jackson had his informal "Kitchen Cabinet," while Franklin D. Roosevelt turned to a group of academics known as his "Brain Trust." The memo also noted that Grover Cleveland consulted financier J.P. Morgan during a Treasury gold shortage, and Lyndon B. Johnson sought advice from trusted friends outside the government during the Vietnam War.

SCHUMER DODGES QUESTIONS AFTER BOMBSHELL REPORT ALLEGES DEM SENATOR HAD RELATIONSHIPS WITH HOUSE STAFFERS

"Yet throughout history, Presidents have relied on private advisers (or, at minimum, advisers outside the Executive Branch) to perform their executive function," Gaiser wrote.

Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., interpreted the Justice Department memo as a sign that Trump is worried about what could come if Democrats win control of Congress.

SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER

"Donald Trump is scared," Schumer wrote on X. "He knows accountability is coming. He’s using his newly installed Attorney General/personal lawyer, Todd Blanche, to cover up his communications with private advisers and special interest cronies.

"These are the actions of someone with something to hide," Schumer continued. "And it shows he is petrified of the questions a Democratic Congress will demand answers to. We will not let Trump escape the accountability he deserves."

Fox News anchor and senior White House correspondent Jacqui Heinrich, who is the new president of the WHCA, sent an "off-the-record" memo to members on Tuesday after meeting with Trump administration officials to discuss the incident. 

TRUMP USED CATERING TRUCK, AIR FORCE ONE DECOY TO EVADE IRAN THREAT: REPORT

"I want members to know what WHCA has done since the story was published. Immediately after it broke, we spoke with members who were on the flight and heard from a number of managers and pool chairs about the broader concerns raised by the report, including press safety, the ability of the pool to maintain an independent record of the president’s movements, and the integrity and credibility of pooled reporting," Heinrich wrote in the letter obtained by Fox News Digital. 

Heinrich said she had a "candid and productive meeting" with senior administration staffers to convey those concerns directly.

"I emphasized that WHCA recognizes the paramount responsibility of the Secret Service to protect the president and that genuine security threats can require extraordinary measures, including circumstances in which operational security limits what can be shared with reporters in real time," Heinrich wrote. 

"At the same time, I advocated strongly for the importance of maintaining independent press coverage of the president and an accurate historical record of his movements," she continued. "I also raised the longer-term implications for the credibility of the pool."

Heinrich wants to ensure that reporters would be able to correct the record once a security concern has passed if there is ever another circumstance in which they "unwittingly" transmit inaccurate or misleading information.

"Otherwise, reporters could be left with reasonable questions about whether information they independently observe and report can be relied upon. That would generate unnecessary uncertainty for both the press corps and the White House," Heinrich wrote. 

WHITE HOUSE NOT DENYING REPORT TRUMP SWITCHED PLANES TO AVOID IRANIAN PLOT

"More broadly, I stressed that undermining confidence in the reliability of pool reports carries risks beyond any single incident," she added. "In an already conspiratorial information environment, uncertainty about whether independent reporting can be trusted can be exploited by bad actors seeking to sow confusion and undermine confidence in journalism."

Heinrich said she asked the White House to work with the WHCA on a protocol for "handling extraordinary security circumstances in the future," while recognizing "the Secret Service’s responsibility to respond to genuine threats while protecting press safety, preserving independent coverage of the president, and providing a mechanism to correct the record after the fact when necessary."

The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment. 

The saga began when the Post reported that Trump secretly boarded a U.S. military aircraft using an airport catering truck as cover to depart the NATO summit in Turkey in July while using an older Air Force One jet as a decoy. 

Following U.S. military strikes against Iranian targets earlier in the summer, intelligence officials identified a specific threat from Iran targeting the president's movements. To counter the threat, U.S. security officials executed a ruse on the Turkish tarmac.

Trump walked up the stairs of the legacy blue-and-white Boeing 747 — the older Air Force One — and waved to news cameras before entering the cabin. Minutes later, Trump and a small team of aides were said to have stepped out of view into an airport catering truck that had been lifted to an exit door on the far side of the plane.

HERE'S WHAT YOU MISSED FROM TRUMP'S FIRST WHCA DINNER AS PRESIDENT: 5 TAKEAWAYS FROM HIS NIGHT WITH THE PRESS

The truck lowered to ground level and drove across the tarmac to a nearby Air Force C-32A, a modified Boeing 757. Meanwhile, the media and White House staff boarded the older 747, unaware that the Secret Service removed Trump from their flight. 

Reporters were then instructed to close their window shades for takeoff, and the jet took off as a decoy, according to the Post. Trump then flew in secrecy aboard the smaller C-32A to RAF Mildenhall in England, landing shortly before the decoy jet.

Last month, Trump attended the annual WHCA Dinner that was rescheduled from its original April 25 date after a crazed gunman stormed the venue.

Fox News Digital’s Emma Bussey contributed to this report.

item.title: Ukraine pounds Black Sea Fleet’s ‘last major stronghold’ while Putin flexes naval power in Pacific
item.description: Putin threatened to seize European vessels from the Russian Black Sea to the Pacific after Ukraine's drone attack crippled Novorossiysk grain terminals.
item.content:encoded:
Russian President Vladimir Putin threatened Wednesday to seize European vessels in retaliation if European countries begin seizing Russian merchant ships after Ukraine launched a major overnight attack on a key Russian Black Sea naval and commercial hub and Moscow staged large-scale war games in the Pacific.

The developments underscore a growing battle at sea: Ukraine is hitting one of Russia’s most important Black Sea naval and export hubs, while Moscow is warning it could seize European vessels and flexing its naval power in the Pacific. Though the events are not directly linked, they show how the war is increasingly extending beyond the front lines into strategic ports and international shipping routes.

Ukraine hammered the port city of Novorossiysk in a massive overnight drone attack that put two major grain terminals out of operation, according to Russian industry sources cited by Reuters Aug. 12. Novorossiysk is a major Black Sea export hub and also serves as a base for Russian warships that Moscow relocated there after repeated Ukrainian attacks on its Black Sea Fleet in Crimea.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy claimed responsibility Wednesday morning for an operation targeting the Novorossiysk naval base, calling it "the last major stronghold of the Russian fleet in the Black Sea." In a post on X, Zelenskyy said Ukraine used Palianytsia jet-powered drones, Neptune missiles and unmanned naval systems and claimed hits on air-defense positions, piers and port infrastructure.

UKRAINE LAUNCHES WHAT APPEARS TO BE ONE OF ITS LARGEST DRONE ATTACKS AGAINST RUSSIA: REPORT

"The occupation fleet and all the infrastructure supporting it will not be safe as long as Russian aggression continues," Zelenskyy wrote.

The governor of Russia’s Krasnodar region said at least two people, including an 8-year-old child, were killed in the wider wave of attacks. Novorossiysk Mayor Andrei Kravchenko said more than two dozen residential buildings, four businesses and educational facilities were damaged, and the city’s water supply was suspended. Reuters reported that Chicago wheat futures rose roughly 3% amid concerns over potential disruptions to Russian grain exports.

Separately Wednesday, thousands of miles to the east, Putin appeared aboard the Russian missile cruiser Varyag near Sakhalin while observing Pacific Fleet exercises and issued a warning to European governments increasingly targeting Russia’s so-called shadow fleet.

The European Union has expanded sanctions against hundreds of vessels and detained some ships and their crews for checks, while some European governments are considering tougher maritime enforcement against vessels suspected of sanctions evasion, Reuters reported Wednesday.

REPORT WARNS RUSSIA USING SHADOW FLEET TO PROBE NATO DRONE DEFENSES

Quoting Putin, Russia’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs wrote on X, "Attempts to seize Russian vessels & sell off our property are outright piracy. If such plans are implemented, Russia will respond in kind – wherever we deem necessary, including within the Pacific Fleet’s area of responsibility."

The warning came against the backdrop of sweeping Russian naval exercises. The drills stretched across the Sea of Japan, Sea of Okhotsk and Northwest Pacific and involved more than 13,000 personnel and around 60 ships, submarines and support vessels. Russian Defense Ministry figures reported separately put the number of participating aircraft, helicopters and unmanned systems at around 30.

Video supplied by East2West showed Russian forces firing anti-ship missiles during the drills. Bastion coastal missile systems launched Oniks cruise missiles at simulated enemy ships from Kamchatka and the Kuril Islands, while the corvette Smerch fired a Uran anti-ship cruise missile, according to East2West.

Putin also used his Pacific appearance to accuse NATO of expanding its presence in the Asia-Pacific and Arctic regions, pointing to new military alliances and planned weapons deployments that he said were increasing the potential for conflict.

RUSSIA PREPARING HYBRID ATTACKS ON NATO'S EASTERN FLANK, INTELLIGENCE WARNS

The developments unfolded as attacks continued on both sides. Reuters reported that Russia struck the Ukrainian port of Odesa and that a separate Russian attack set fire to a shopping mall in Zaporizhzhia, underscoring the continuing pressure on ports and logistics infrastructure as the war approaches four and a half years.

Separately, Romania said its naval forces destroyed two suspected Russian Gerbera drones over the Black Sea, roughly 90 nautical miles from Constanta, according to East2West.

NATO said its North Atlantic Council met Wednesday to discuss Russian airspace violations in Poland and Romania and recent drone incidents. A NATO spokesperson said allies "condemned Russia for actions, expressed solidarity with allies affected [and] reaffirmed support to Ukraine."

Reuters contributed to this report.

item.title: 8-year-old boy reels in bizarre surprise during weekend fishing trip at Pennsylvania lake
item.description: Seamus Coffey was fishing for bass in Pennsylvania's Ridley Park Lake when he reeled in a piranha, later confirmed by the state Fish and Boat Commission.
item.content:encoded:
An 8-year-old boy went fishing for bass and catfish in Pennsylvania over the weekend and instead hauled in something that belongs roughly 4,000 miles farther south.

A piranha.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Seamus Coffey was fishing with his dad, Michael, at Ridley Park Lake on Saturday when something grabbed his line. At first, Seamus figured he had hooked a bass.

"I'm reeling it in, and I think there's a bass," Seamus told 6ABC Philadelphia.

His dad could tell pretty quickly, though, that this was not one of their usual catches.

"I was like, 'Slow down dude, you might lose it.' This looks like something we haven't caught before," Michael recalled.

Once the fish hit dry land, Dad was still trying to figure out what exactly they were looking at.

Seamus, meanwhile, apparently needed about three seconds.

"He said, 'It's a piranha!'" Michael said.

How did he know that?

"Because I watch YouTube!" Seamus said.

Michael pulled up photos on Google and came to the same conclusion, and the Pennsylvania Fish and Boat Commission later confirmed that the roughly 9.5-inch, 2-pound fish was indeed some species of piranha.

Piranhas are native to South America, not suburban Philadelphia, so state officials have a pretty good idea how this one arrived at Ridley Park Lake: Somebody likely dumped a pet they no longer wanted.

Pennsylvania Fish and Boat Commission spokesperson Mike Parker said exotic animals can seem like a great idea when they're small, only for owners to eventually realize that housing, feeding and caring for them can become expensive and difficult.

Dumping them into a nearby lake, however, is not the solution.

"That is probably the worst thing you can do for an animal that's been a pet," Parker said.

It's also illegal. Pennsylvania prohibits releasing exotic species into the wild, and violators can face fines or prosecution.

Michael said he initially returned the fish to the water before reconsidering and ultimately disposed of it humanely. Parker said removing it was the right call because a non-native fish could pose a risk to people and disrupt the local ecosystem.

LARGEMOUTH BASS EXPLODES FROM WATER TO EAT CHARL SCHWARTZEL'S GOLF BALL AT LIV GOLF NEW YORK

Parker said this particular fish likely wouldn't have survived long outside its natural habitat anyway, especially after presumably spending its life as a pet.

And, bizarrely enough, Pennsylvania has been through this before.

In July 2016, a woman and her son hooked a red-bellied piranha at North Park Lake near Pittsburgh. That fish managed to flip back into the water after the anglers removed the hook. Officials at the time also suspected someone had released an unwanted aquarium fish and said Pennsylvania's cold weather would eventually take care of the problem.

Ten years later, another Pennsylvania kid has a piranha story of his own.

And despite unexpectedly finding a mouthful of razor-sharp teeth on the end of his line, Seamus doesn't appear traumatized in the slightest.

"Fishing is my favorite thing," he said.

After Saturday, though, it's going to be pretty tough for the next bluegill to impress him.

item.title: Peggy Flanagan was Minnesota's No 2 official as massive fraud scandal exploded under state's watch
item.description: Minnesota Lt. Gov. Peggy Flanagan just scored the Democratic nomination for Senate, but she's hampered by some heavy baggage: her role during the Minnesota fraud scandal.
item.content:encoded:
Minnesota's new Democratic nominee for Senate has baggage heading into the November election: the massive fraud scandal that rippled through the Land of 10,000 Lakes happened right under her nose.  

Lt. Gov. Peggy Flanagan scored a major win for the insurgent progressive movement that's reshaping the Democratic Party from the outside on Tuesday, toppling the more moderate Rep. Angie Craig, D-Minn., in the process. But her role during the Minnesota fraud scandal has plagued her campaign, with both sides attacking her on the issue. 

It became Craig's prime line of attack against her. 

"The lieutenant governor, even as we sit here today, continues to take absolutely no accountability for any of the fraud issues, and she continues to blame the governor," Craig said during a debate with Flanagan on Minnesota Public Radio. "And I'm going to be honest: It's pissing me off."

PEGGY FLANAGAN VOWS TO 'RIP ICE APART' AFTER TOPPLING MODERATE DEM IN KEY SENATE BATTLE

During the campaign, Craig charged that Flanagan had largely shrugged off responsibility for the fraud scandal, despite having served alongside Walz as his No. 2 since the pair were first elected in 2018. 

In an interview with the Minnesota Reformer, Flanagan said, "The governor has said that the buck stops with him, and he took the lead here," on the fraud scandal. 

Notably, Flanagan did not mention fraud during her victory speech Tuesday night, instead focusing on hallmarks of her campaign thus far, such as vowing to "rip [Immigration and Customs Enforcement] apart" following the deadly shootings in Minnesota earlier this year. 

Still, the scandal torpedoed Walz's re-election hopes, and Republicans plan to lean into it in the weeks leading up to Nov. 3. 

HALL OF FAMER TONY DUNGY ENDORSES MICHELE TAFOYA IN CROWDED MINNESOTA REPUBLICAN PRIMARY FOR U.S. SENATE

Her opponent, former NFL sideline reporter Michele Tafoya, has already pounced on the opportunity several times this election season and did so again shortly after being crowned the Republican nominee for Senate. 

"Minnesotans of every political stripe are fed up. They're exhausted with this fraud," Tafoya told a Minnesota Fox affiliate.

"We cannot show our children that failure comes without accountability," she continued. "We've got to have accountability, but more than that, we've got to do things, everything we do, to make Minnesota more livable, more affordable, more safe, and without fraud, and we're gonna do that."

National Republicans are confident that she could win big in November.

While Minnesota is not on the NRSC’s target map of eight battleground seats, Sen. Tim Scott, R-S.C., who chairs the committee, believes Tafoya is a serious contender to Democrats, who have held both Senate seats since 2009.

"The one thing that gets me excited when I think about this election cycle on the map is Minnesota," Scott told CNN. "I think Minnesota, we have a real shot with Michele Tafoya."

REPUBLICANS GET THE DEMOCRAT THEY WANTED AS SOCIALIST ABDUL EL-SAYED WINS MICHIGAN SENATE PRIMARY

Republicans also see Tafoya’s more moderate leanings as a positive heading into November.

A GOP operative told Fox News Digital that she’s seen as a candidate who can unite swing, moderate and MAGA voters in a winning coalition.

"Tafoya has the power to appeal to a broader electorate that’s starving for authenticity," the operative said. "Her career as a sideline reporter for NBC’s ‘Sunday Night Football’ makes her relatable to a mainstream crowd."

Her position on abortion, for example, could attract swing voters.

In an open letter to Minnesotans, Tafoya wrote that, as a senator, she would oppose taxpayer-funded abortions, support conservative, strict-constructionist judges and remain "completely aligned with President Donald Trump on this issue." She also expressed support for the Dobbs decision.

But she won’t support a total ban on abortion.

"I do not support an outright ban on abortion, and I believe there should be reasonable access in the first 12 weeks of pregnancy," Tafoya wrote. "Further, I believe that states who restrict access to fertility treatments like IVF are also acting wrongly — being pro-family is pro-life."

item.title: Former 'Real Housewives' star calls Andy Cohen's political take defending 'MAGA' women 'full of s---'
item.description: Former "RHOC" star Kelly Dodd claimed Andy Cohen was "full of s---" for defending MAGA women on Bravo, claiming they weren't welcome on the show.
item.content:encoded:
Former "Real Housewives of Orange County" star Kelly Dodd claimed Bravo host Andy Cohen was "full of s---" Tuesday after he defended the inclusion of "MAGA women" on the show.

Dodd spoke to Fox News Digital after the "Watch What Happens Live" host was asked on Threads why there were "so many MAGA women" on the series, particularly the "Orange County" season.

"If we didn’t showcase people with different POV’s there would be no show. Also it’s a show about the women and their relationships, not about politics," Cohen wrote on Sunday.

KELLY DODD FIRES BACK AT CANCEL CULTURE, SAYS SHE'S TREATED LIKE 'AN OUTCAST' IN HOLLYWOOD

Dodd called out this comment, claiming Cohen and Bravo did not care for conservative perspectives on the show before and have since become concerned only about ratings.

"They're making excuses that they need points of view when I don't think that's true," Dodd said. "He doesn't have different points of view. I think he's full of s---."

Dodd pointed to Cohen's past comments attacking conservatives and right-leaning perspectives and viewed his Threads comment and described the suggestion that the show was welcoming different types of women as disingenuous.

"I think that he sees that the ratings are slipping, and he needs to get back some conservative. He's lost half of his audience. Any time you talk, speak about politics. ... you're gonna p--- off half the country," Dodd said.

ANDY COHEN BLASTS JOE ROGAN AS A 'F---ING IDIOT' AFTER HE BACKS PRATT FOR LA MAYOR

Cohen, however, agreed that the "Real Housewives" brand was not political in any way and that she had not discussed politics prior to the COVID-19 pandemic.

"The show is not about politics. It's about women's lives. It's not about politics. No one's running for office,s or no one's talking about politics," Dodd said.

Bravo and its parent company NBCUniversal declined to comment. 

Fox News Digital also reached out to Cohen's representative for comment but did not immediately hear back.

Dodd was among multiple women who were fired or left the franchise after making controversial comments or criticizing left-wing politics. Dodd was fired from the series in 2021 after controversial remarks about the COVID-19 pandemic and accusations of her mocking the Black Lives Matter movement. 

REALITY STAR SAYS 'RHOC' COST HER MARRIAGE AS DAUGHTER SHUNS SHOW AFTER MILITARY HUSBAND'S PORTRAYAL

Former cast member Annemarie Wiley of "The Real Housewives of Beverly Hills" also spoke to Fox News Digital last year about no longer being invited to the show after leaving in 2024 for expressing conservative views, like protecting girls sports.

"I was given a terrible edit by Bravo, and I found out after the season was finished when they didn't invite me back that that was the reason that I was given that edit, apparently … because I was a conservative," Wiley told Fox News Digital.

Earlier this year, NBCUniversal boasted that Bravo was "a top cable entertainment network among key female demos" with Q1 2026 scoring Bravo's biggest quarter on the streaming service Peacock.

However, seasons of the "Real Housewives" franchise have reportedly seen declining ratings in recent years.

item.title: John Hinckley Jr gives his thoughts on Jodie Foster 45 years after shooting Ronald Reagan to impress her
item.description: John Hinckley Jr. reveals that Jodie Foster could have been a target herself, saying "fate went the other way" toward former President Ronald Reagan.
item.content:encoded:
John Hinckley Jr., the man who shot former President Ronald Reagan in 1981 to impress Jodie Foster, said he wants nothing but good things for the actress.

"I just wish Jodie Foster well," he said. "I don’t really see her movies, but I wish her well, and I know she’s doing quite well. And that’s all I can say: I just, I wish Jodie well, and I hope she has a good life."

The 71-year-old explained on the "Mark Joseph Show" in an exclusive preview shared with Entertainment Weekly that when he shot Reagan 45 years ago in a delusional state, he believed he would spend the rest of his life with the "Silence of the Lambs" actress.

REAGAN SHOOTER CALLS LINK TO WASHINGTON HOTEL ‘SPOOKY’ AFTER ALLEGED TRUMP ASSASSINATION ATTEMPT AT SAME SITE

The full episode will air on Wednesday.

"I wanted to have like this union with Jodie Foster and live the rest of my life with her and all these things that, of course, were delusional, but I was believing those things at that time. So, the best outcome would have been to just have like this union with Jodie Foster," Hinckley told Joseph after the host asked what he believed at the time would be the best thing that could come out of the shooting.

He explained that he believed at the time that Foster would "join me wherever I was. You know, I didn’t know if I was going to be in jail or hospital or what, but after things settled down, I had this notion that she was going to join me wherever I was."

It came out shortly after Hinckley’s assassination attempt that left Reagan with a broken rib, punctured lung and internal bleeding, that Hinckley was obsessed with Foster after seeing her in "Taxi Driver" and thought the shooting would make her notice him.

JODIE FOSTER HAUNTED BY HORRIFIC DOG TRAGEDY, BELIEVES SHE GAVE UP WHAT SHE LOVES MOST FOR SUCCESS

Hinckley was found not guilty by reason of insanity after shooting the former president outside the Washington Hilton two months after he was elected.

Former White House press secretary James Brady was shot in the head and suffered brain damage and partial paralysis, which led to his death in 2014. His death was ruled a homicide.

Two other men were also wounded in the shooting.

Hinckley was committed to a psychiatric hospital after the trial and released in 2016. By 2022, he was living in Virginia without any court restrictions.

Hinckley admitted to Joseph, however, that, in his delusional state, Foster could have been a target herself.

"She definitely could have been a target. It’s just fate went the other way," Hinckley said. "But, yeah, she could have been a target. But, as fate turned out, it was Reagan instead of her."

In a 2022 interview with CBS, Hinckley apologized for his actions.

"I shot four people, and I’m sorry to the Reagan family, the Brady family, the other families of the victims," he said at the time. "I’m sorry to Jodie Foster for bringing her into this."

item.title: Mamdani's team said NYPD would accompany his wife on Middle East vacation — cops say that's not true
item.description: The NYPD denied it would send officers to Syria and Lebanon with Rama Duwaji, contradicting Mayor Zohran Mamdani's office on the security detail.
item.content:encoded:
The New York Police Department (NYPD) will not provide a security detail to Mayor Zohran Mamdani's wife during her upcoming vacation to two terror hotspots in the Middle East, despite the mayor's office claiming otherwise.

"The NYPD does not send officers to countries with level 4 travel advisories for discretionary reasons such as personal travel," a spokesperson for the law enforcement agency told Fox News.

Mamdani's wife, Rama Duwaji, is planning to travel to Syria and Lebanon to visit family in September, according to the New York Post. Both of those countries are on the State Department's "Do Not Travel" list due to terrorism concerns.

MAMDANI'S WIFE CO-HOSTS LUXE MUSLIM RETREAT CASTING VIRGIN MARY AS ‘PALESTINIAN WOMAN’ UNDER OCCUPATION

The mayor's office had previously confirmed that Duwaji would have an NYPD security detail on the trip.

"Upon the strong recommendation of the NYPD, the first lady’s security detail will be joining her when she travels to visit family in Syria and Lebanon," Mamdani’s spokeswoman Dora Pekec reportedly said.

But later, as it became clear that the NYPD would not be making the overseas trek, the mayor chalked the confusion up to a staff "miscommunication" when asked about it by news outlet PIX11 on Tuesday.

NYPD Detectives’ Endowment Association (DEA) President Scott Munro furiously slammed the implication that NYPD detectives would accompany the city's First Lady to the Middle East.

MAMDANI CLASHES WITH DEMOCRATIC SOCIALISTS' PUSH TO ABOLISH POLICE AND PRISONS

"Our detectives put themselves in harm’s way every day protecting New Yorkers," said Munro. "The DEA would never remain silent if our members were asked to travel to a dangerous, off-limits foreign country for anything other than a legitimate law-enforcement or intelligence operation."

"Our detectives are needed here in New York City protecting residents and fighting crime," he added.

Mamdani has a long history of trashing the very police department he thought would accompany and provide security for his wife to the dangerous Middle Eastern countries on New York City taxpayer's dime.

"There is no negotiating with an institution this wicked & corrupt. Defund it. Dismantle it. End the cycle of violence," Mamdani said in reference to the NYPD in a viral 2020 post on X.

"We don't need an investigation to know that the NYPD is racist, anti-queer & a major threat to public safety," he said in another 2020 post, adding in a follow-up: "What we need is to #DefundTheNYPD."

JON STEWART PRESSES MAMDANI ON WHERE HE BREAKS WITH FELLOW DEMOCRATIC SOCIALISTS ON PRISONS AND BORDERS

"Queer liberation means defund the police," he said in yet another post.

The mayor, who has also faced scrutiny for his anti-Israel views and recently called Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu a "war criminal" while calling for his arrest, derogatorily linked the NYPD to the Israeli Defense Forces (IDF).

"We have to make clear that when the boot of the NYPD is on your neck, it’s been laced by the IDF," Mamdani, who was a keynote speaker, said during a panel discussion at the Democratic Socialists of America's 2023 national convention.

During his campaign for mayor of the most populated U.S. city, Mamdani said the exact opposite, explicitly stating that he did not want to defund the police.

SEE IT: MAMDANI BOOED OFF STAGE AT NEW YORK CITY PRO-POLICE CELEBRATION: ‘WALKED OFF IN SHAME’

Still, it appears there is no love lost between Mamdani and the NYPD.

Just last week, he was booed offstage when he tried to speak at a pro-police event in Staten Island.

Fox News Digital reached out to Mamdani's office for comment.
